title: Adaptive context-window sweeper and cache-entropy reporter
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Introduce an automated context-window sweep harness and a cache-entropy reporter to surface KV-cache effectiveness across sequence lengths. Useful for identifying knee points for prefetching and cache sizing.
description:
Summary: Adds a new benchmark harness (context-window sweeper) that exercises models with systematically increasing context windows and priming prefixes to measure throughput, p95/p99 latency, GPU memory pressure, KV-cache hit/entropy, and tail amplification. Also adds a small Go reporter that consumes sweeper telemetry and emits a compact per-model per-length entropy surface used by Optimize heuristics.

Motivation: We often observe non-linear drops in throughput as context grows, but we lack a compact, reproducible reporter that correlates KV-cache entropy (how much of the prefix is re-used) with latency/throughput. This PR provides a reproducible sweep and an entropy reporter that can be hooked into the nightly profiling pipeline.

Design:
- context-window sweeper runner (Python): accepts a sequence length schedule, primer set, concurrency pattern and runs batched requests against local bench model endpoints. Supports warmup priming, deterministic tokenization seeds and KV-cache checkpointing.
- entropy reporter (Go): ingests the sweeper's JSON trace stream and computes per-length "cache entropy" (Shannon-style) and a normalized reuse score. Produces CSV/JSON maps and a compact heatmap artifact.
- integration test harness: a lightweight synthetic model shim that simulates predictable reuse patterns to validate entropy computation.
- CI job: bench/context-sweep.yml to run a fast smoke sweep on PRs and a nightly full sweep runner.

Review conversation (chronological, condensed):
- Alex Chen (reviewer): "Nice focused tool; two high-level asks: 1) make the entropy metric explicit in the docs (units and normalization), 2) add a small guard in the runner to avoid memory blowup when the primer set is large."
- Priya (author): "Addressed both: added docs section 'entropy math' and a streaming primer iterator to keep memory O(batch). Also added an optional sample cap flag."
- Jordan Lee (reviewer): "Found a race in the async tokenizer when running with concurrency=8 on my laptop; failing test reproduced in entropy_test. Please ensure deterministic seeding in the synthetic shim."
- Priya: "Fixed race, added deterministic RNG seeding and an integration test that runs with concurrency 12 to catch regressions."
- Samir Patel (approver): "Benchmarks look stable locally; CI smoke job passed after the fixes. Approving for merge."

CI notes:
- Initial CI run: bench smoke job failed on entropy_test (race) on macos-latest
- Rerun after a8f3dba fixed race: all bench jobs passed (smoke + unit + quick integration).
- Nightly job added to pipeline but is gated to separate runner.

Observability:
- The reporter emits the following metrics (paginated in output CSV and annotated JSON): length, requests, avg_latency_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, gpu_mem_mb_avg, kvcache_hit_rate, cache_entropy_bits.
- Heatmap artifact example included at bench-data/sweeps/example_heatmap_v0.json

Performance notes from local runs (attached in PR artifact):
- Small models: throughput stable until ~512 tokens, then linear degradation
- Medium models: sharp knee at 1024 tokens correlated with cache_entropy > 6.2 bits
- Observed memory pressure spikes when concurrent warmup priming threads > 6, addressed with sampler throttle

Usage & next steps:
- Hook the producer to nightly profiling to collect per-model entropy surfaces across the catalog.
- Integrate entropy surface into Optimize engine to suggest prefetch/pinning thresholds.
- Add a visualization in Console (follow-up ENG-4905) to display heatmaps and automatic knee suggestions.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI. Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in runtime changes (no changes to the serving runtime itself) — it is a user-space benchmark + reporter to guide future runtime tuning.

Tests: unit tests for entropy math, integration smoke that exercises runner+reporter against synthetic shim, and a short e2e in CI that validates the produced heatmap file structure.

Related: ENG-4821 (bench infra track), ENG-4905 (Optimize integration follow-up).
notes: This PR was created as part of the benchmark lab initiative to produce more explainable signals for batching/prefetch heuristics. Artifacts attached: sample heatmap JSON and raw trace ndjson (small).
